correctness.rationale: The posterior information matrix P^{-1}+r^{-1}hh^T has trace independent of h in dimension two. Its condition number strictly decreases with its determinant at fixed trace, and the matrix determinant lemma reduces maximal determinant to the simple largest-eigenvalue Rayleigh quotient; hence exactly h=±u_L minimizes conditioning. The posterior variances are Lr/(L+r), mu; division yields q=Lr/[mu(L+r)] and condition max(q,1/q). Solving q=1 gives r*=Lmu/(L-mu), while q<1/(L/mu) is equivalent to r<Lmu^2/(L^2-mu^2). Normalization ||h||=1, positive r and strict L>mu are necessary; exact (4,1) example checks r*=4/3 and r=1/4 gives 17/4. This is an analytic all-parameter proof, not finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: The result is only 2-dimensional, one scalar measurement, unit direction, fixed prior and Gaussian independent noise; no state prediction or sensor library is analyzed.
The packaged verifier checks finite rational cases, not a universal statement.
